backend/servers/api-server/src/services/accounting.rs:124-176 — the payment auto-matcher's inner `for invoice in &open_invoices` loop (accounting.rs:129) creates a `PaymentMatch` for EVERY invoice whose confidence reaches the 0.5 threshold, with NO `break` after the first accepted match and NO in-memory update of `line.match_state`.

The outer per-line guard (`if line.match_state != "unmatched" && line.match_state != "suggested" { continue }`, accounting.rs:125-126) reads the DB-loaded `line` copy, which is never mutated inside the loop. The DB `update_bank_statement_line_match_state_rls(... "suggested")` call (accounting.rs:170) does not touch the local `line`, so subsequent iterations of the SAME line keep matching. Result: one bank statement line is suggested-matched to multiple invoices in a single pass.

Reachable precondition: two or more open invoices (status Issued/PartiallyPaid) that share the same non-empty `variable_symbol`. Variable Symbol alone contributes 0.8 (accounting.rs:135-138) which crosses the 0.5 acceptance threshold, so every open invoice carrying that VS produces a duplicate `PaymentMatch` (state Suggested) for the one incoming payment. Nothing in the schema enforces VS uniqueness across open invoices (partial payments, reissues, tenant data-entry errors make collisions plausible).

Consequence: duplicate/conflicting suggested matches for a single payment; a manager reconciling the statement sees the same incoming amount proposed against several invoices, and any downstream 'accept highest-confidence per invoice' step could book one payment against multiple invoices.
Fix: `break` after the first accepted match (or select the single best-confidence invoice for the line), and/or mark the line consumed in-memory so later iterations skip it.

backend/servers/api-server/src/services/accounting.rs:135-150 — a Variable-Symbol match alone contributes 0.8 and crosses the 0.5 acceptance threshold (accounting.rs:150) with NO amount corroboration required. So a bank line whose `amount` is wildly different from the invoice's `remaining_amount = total_amount - paid_amount` (accounting.rs:142) — e.g. a large credit against a small invoice, or an amount far exceeding the outstanding balance — is still suggested at 0.8 purely on the VS. routes/sso.rs:731-738 — introspect_pm_token() returns the cached `active` verbatim on a hit and short-circuits before contacting the PM introspection endpoint.

Consequence: a PM access token that is revoked upstream (user logs out of PM / admin revokes) or that expires within the caching window is still treated as `active=true` by reality-server for up to the full 60s TTL after revocation/expiry — a stale-auth acceptance window on the SSO validation path. Fix: bound each cache entry's expires_at by min(ttl, token_exp - now) and/or invalidate on logout.

backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/sso.rs:682 (exchange_code_for_tokens), :706 (get_user_info), :743 (introspect_pm_token) each build a fresh `reqwest::Client::new()` and call `.send()` with NO `.timeout()`. reqwest's default client has no request timeout, so the outbound call can block indefinitely.

These are all on the auth-critical SSO path (OAuth callback token exchange, userinfo fetch, and token introspection). A slow or hung PM OAuth/introspection endpoint stalls the awaiting handler for as long as the upstream keeps the socket open, pinning the tokio task/connection and enabling upstream-induced resource exhaustion.

The codebase already has the correct pattern: state.rs:757-760 `PmApiClient::new` builds its client via `reqwest::Client::builder().timeout(Duration::from_secs(timeout_seconds)).build()`. The SSO helpers bypass it and also skip connection-pool reuse by minting a new client per request. Fix: reuse a shared client with an explicit `.timeout(...)` (and connect timeout) for all three PM calls.

backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/sso.rs:753-762 — introspect_pm_token() treats ANY non-2xx introspection response as an inactive token: `if !response.status().is_success() { state.token_cache.set(token, false, None, None).await; return Err(...) }`. This does not distinguish an authoritative `401/200 active:false` from a transient upstream failure (500/502/503/504).

When the PM introspection endpoint has a transient outage or 5xx blip, a VALID user token is negatively cached as `active=false` for the full 60s TTL (state.rs:735-748). Because get() serves that cached `active=false` (sso.rs:731-738), the legitimate user keeps getting rejected for up to 60s AFTER the PM API has already recovered.

Consequence: an availability defect that amplifies a brief upstream hiccup into a 60s per-token lockout. Fix: only negative-cache authoritative inactive results (2xx with active=false, or 401); on 5xx/transport errors return an error WITHOUT caching (fail-open to a re-introspection, not a cached deny).

frontend/apps/reality-web/src/components/listings/LayoutSections.tsx — `SectionBoundary` (a minimal class error boundary wrapping every listing-detail layout section) implements `componentDidCatch(_error, _info)` with an empty body and the comment `// Intentionally swallowed — console.error suppressed by tests` (~:68). backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/listings.rs:338 — in `get_listing` (the tenant-scoped GET /api/v1/listings/{id} detail handler, listings.rs:316-345), the photos sub-fetch swallows all repository errors: `let photos = state.listing_repo.get_photos(id).await.unwrap_or_default();`. `.unwrap_or_default()` collapses an `Err(sqlx/pool error)` into an empty `Vec`, which is indistinguishable from 'this listing genuinely has no photos'.

There is no `tracing::warn!`/`error!` on the swallowed branch, so the failure is invisible in logs and cannot be monitored — same fail-quiet class as the previously-tracked quiet-hours `.ok()` swallow, but on a user-facing read path. backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/integrations/webhook.rs:201-203 (create_webhook_subscription) and :337-339 (update path) derive the SSRF-guard mode as `let is_production = std::env::var("RUST_ENV").map(|v| v == "production").unwrap_or(false);`. This value is passed to `integration_repo.create_webhook_subscription(..., is_production)` (:207), which forwards it to `validate_webhook_url(&data.url, is_production)` at backend/crates/db/src/repositories/integration.rs:1352.

The env detection FAILS OPEN and is INVERTED relative to every other RUST_ENV gate in the same binary. `.unwrap_or(false)` plus an exact `== "production"` match means: RUST_ENV unset, or set to anything other than the literal string `"production"` (e.g. `prod`, `PRODUCTION`, `staging`, or simply not configured) => `is_production = false` => the webhook-URL validator runs in relaxed/dev mode. Every other environment gate in the crate uses the SAFE convention `RUST_ENV == "development"` and defaults to strict when unset: main.rs:483/533/539, services/totp.rs:58, preflight.rs:125, and notably services/actions/api_call.rs:339 (its sibling outbound-request SSRF guard, 'plain-http gated to RUST_ENV=development'). webhook.rs is the lone site that keys strict behavior off `== "production"`, so it is the only guard that turns OFF when the var is unset.

Impact: in validate_webhook_url (backend/crates/db/src/models/integration.rs:887-903, 932-937) the localhost/loopback block is gated on is_production — `is_localhost` (localhost / 127.0.0.1 / ::1) is only rejected when is_production is true (:901), and the 127.0.0.0/8 branch is `if octets[0] == 127 && (is_production || !is_localhost)` (:933), and plain `http://` is permitted for localhost when `!is_production` (:891). Private ranges (10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16), link-local 169.254/16 (cloud metadata) and multicast are blocked unconditionally, so residual reach is loopback-scoped. Net: an authenticated org member can register a webhook subscription targeting `http://localhost:<port>` / `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` / `http://[::1]:<port>`; the server later delivers signed POSTs to it (webhook.rs:572-584 computes the HMAC and fires the request), yielding an SSRF primitive against loopback-bound services co-located with api-server (Redis 6379, metrics/admin ports, internal-only HTTP) whenever RUST_ENV is not exactly `production`.

RUST_ENV is NOT listed in backend/CLAUDE.md's env table nor in any .env.example, and no other code path requires it to be set to `production` in prod (they only ever check for `development`). So a standard prod deployment that leaves RUST_ENV unset silently ships with the loopback SSRF guard disabled. Fix: invert to the crate's safe convention — compute `is_production = std::env::var("RUST_ENV").unwrap_or_default() != "development"` (fail closed / strict by default), or better, hoist a single shared `is_development()`/`is_production()` helper so this can't drift again, and consider always applying the loopback block regardless of env.

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/ai/voice.rs:165-176 (exchange_voice_oauth_tokens, called from link_voice_device :80): when `VoiceOAuthManager::from_env()` reports the platform is not configured (`!oauth_manager.has_platform(voice_platform)`), the handler logs a warn and `return Ok((None, None, None))` — it then creates a persisted voice device row (:89-109) with NULL access/refresh tokens and responds `201 CREATED` with `oauth_linked: false` (:122-131). Lower severity than a security bug: no data exposure, and the client can observe `oauth_linked:false`. But it is a genuine prod-vs-dev fail-open completeness gap. Fix: gate the token-less fallback on a development check (mirror ai/llm.rs:250-263) so an unconfigured voice OAuth manager returns 503 NOT_CONFIGURED in production rather than persisting a half-linked device.

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/data_residency.rs:1040-1048 — in the data-residency dashboard handler, the top-level `compliance_status` field is computed as `if last_verification.as_ref().map(|v| v.is_compliant).unwrap_or(true) { ComplianceStatus::Compliant } else { ComplianceStatus::NonCompliant }`. backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/data_residency.rs:936-941 — `last_verification` is `None` exactly when `data_residency_repo.get_latest_verification_result(org_id)` returns `None`, i.e. the organization has NEVER run a compliance verification (a fresh org, or one whose verification rows were purged). backend/crates/db/src/repositories/data_residency.rs:552-596 — the current repo implementation always emits `"chain_valid": <bool>`, so today the missing-field branch is not reachable and the practical impact is low. frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/lib/api.ts:213-221 — the axios response interceptor has a reactive 401 hook: `if (error.response?.status === 401 && onUnauthorizedCallback) { onUnauthorizedCallback(); }`. `onUnauthorizedCallback` is a module-level var (api.ts:180) set only from `configureApiClient({ onUnauthorized })` (api.ts:196). Fix: pass `onUnauthorized` into the AuthContext.tsx:337 `configureApiClient` call, routing it to the existing dedup-guarded `refreshToken()` (retry the original request on success, hard-logout + redirect on failure); or add a proactive scheduled refresh keyed off the access-token TTL. backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/agent_reviews.rs:190-269 — create_review (POST /api/v1/realtors/{id}/reviews) lets an authenticated portal principal post a rating+body for realtor_profiles.id = {id}. reviewer_user_id is correctly server-derived from principal.user_id (agent_reviews.rs:263) and rating is bounds-checked 1..=5 (agent_reviews.rs:196-201), but there is NO guard that principal.user_id != the reviewed realtor's owner user_id.
